old: Its name once leaned on an old word for a low, droning sound.
Before its current form, English called it humbul-be.
The name is a mash-up: a buzzing word plus bee, and a drink borrowed the idea from Ukrainian.
clues: This flying insect has a name that absorbed a medieval verb meaning 'to boom, buzz,' so it carries its own soundtrack.
It is a big, fuzzy, round-bodied bee, chunkier and hairier than a honeybee, often seen lumbering between flowers with a deep, lazy drone.
In Middle English it was called a humbul-be, and today it also names a drink, a sense borrowed from a Ukrainian word for this insect.
